question:
**Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:**

The policy aims to neither penalise first-time offenders (1)/ nor those who may have violated norms (2)/ due to systemic ambiguity (3)/ rather than deliberate intent. (4)
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The issue in this sentence is the incorrect placement of the correlative conjunction "neither...nor."
 
• The phrase "neither penalise first-time offenders" should be correctly placed to ensure parallel structure with "nor those who may have violated norms."
 
• The sentence should read: "The policy aims to penalise neither first-time offenders nor those who may have violated norms..."
 
• The error lies in **part 1** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The policy aims **to penalise **neither first-time offenders nor those who may have violated norms due to systemic ambiguity rather than deliberate intent."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "nor those who may have violated norms" is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 3:** "due to systemic ambiguity" is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4:** "rather than deliberate intent" is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
